briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek-R2 escalate frontier race as multi-agent systems near production deployment

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released 9 major models this month with OpenAI and DeepSeek leading capability gains. US export controls are slowing Chinese compute while funding remains robust at $14.9B quarterly. Multi-agent coordination and safety tooling are now the dominant investment themes.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with native multi-agent orchestration; DeepSeek-R2 matched o3 performance on coding benchmarks at 40% lower inference cost. Anthropic Claude 4 Opus and Google Gemini 2.5 Ultra entered public preview this week.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target agent-to-agent authentication while automotive and IoT pilots test protocol-level defenses.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC began volume production of 2nm AI chips; Microsoft announced three new 200MW data center campuses in Texas and Arizona. xAI secured 100k H200 GPUs through a joint venture with CoreWeave.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first multi-agent system to demonstrate sustained autonomous R&D trigger a new round of export controls before 2027?
